title: Cryptic planaria randomize head number per animal, not per cell

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Cryptic planaria randomize head number per animal, not per cell

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Perturbing the planarian bioelectric control circuit produces 'Cryptic' destabilized worms whose fragments, even from the same parent, regenerate one-headed and two-headed forms at a set frequency of about 1:2, yet each animal has clear heads and tails rather than mixed tissue, so the randomized bioelectric state is interpreted by collectives rather than by individual cells.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction › Left/right, head/tail: random, but collective anatomical decisions

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: More specifically, several perturbations targeting the bioelectric control circuit (Fig. 5e) have shown randomization of outcome: such Cryptic planaria are destabilized, and fragments (even from the same parent worm) will form 1-head and 2-head forms at a set frequency of ~1:2130 (Fig. 5f).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: McMillen P, Levin M, “Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates”, Communications biology (2024), doi:10.1038/s42003-024-06037-4; section “Introduction › Left/right, head/tail: random, but collective anatomical decisions”. Scope: Planarians after gap-junction or bioelectric perturbation

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-collective-08: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.67

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Outcome frequencies and within-animal tissue coherence are directly scoreable from suitable images and counts. Existing public reports support these observations, but the collective-level interpretation is not uniquely established.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: From blinded fragment outcomes, estimate one- versus two-headed frequencies within parent worms and quantify whether head/tail identity is coherent or cell-speckled within each regenerated animal.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Coherent anatomy alone does not identify the scale at which randomness entered.

The complete fragment-level dataset may not be open.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Head number per fragment and within-animal coherence are directly scorable, and the source papers report a characteristic one-head to two-head frequency with coherent anatomy. Those counts are not a public raw table. The pattern can be checked from the published tallies for those perturbations, and the further reading that collectives interpret a randomized bioelectric state remains an inference from the absence of speckled tissue.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: After the stated bioelectric perturbations, score regenerates from the same parent as one-headed or two-headed and record whether any individual is a mosaic of head and tail tissue. A stable frequency near one double-headed animal in three, with each animal anatomically coherent, would support collective-level randomization; speckled identity within animals, or a ratio that is not repeatable, would refute the stated pattern.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The roughly 1:2 counts are in the primary figures, not a multi-lab deposited table.

Coherent anatomy shows the outcome is animal-level; it does not show that a bioelectric variable was read by a collective rather than by a gradient.

The ratio is tied to particular gap-junction or voltage perturbations and may not travel.
